summary: c1 is introduced: the old allocation-failure check was satisfied before the helper changed and fails afterward. c2 is introduced: the per-context handler route did not exist before and the unchanged harness cannot select it afterward. The NewRef failure in c1 returns before fallback processing.

claims.necessity_reason: The reviewed execution-compatibility obligation is frozen as necessary; this claim assesses its timing.

before.requirement: For an injected XInclude allocation failure, the existing check must observe XML_ERR_NO_MEMORY through the XInclude context getter.
before.reason: At the NewRef allocation failure, the old helper explicitly sets ctxt->errNo to XML_ERR_NO_MEMORY. The unchanged getter returns that field, satisfying the harness check.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: NewRef invokes the old helper when its allocation fails.
The getter exposes the context errNo field used by the harness check.

after.requirement: For the same injected XInclude allocation failure, the existing check must observe XML_ERR_NO_MEMORY through the XInclude context getter.
after.reason: The new helper passes a null optional error structure to xmlRaiseMemoryError, which sets the global error but does not set ctxt->errNo. NewRef returns null before fallback loading, and the getter still reads ctxt->errNo, so the harness aborts on the mismatch.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The called helper updates the global error and updates an optional error structure only when its pointer is nonnull.
NewRef invokes the changed helper and returns null on the selected allocation failure.
ExpandNode returns on AddNode failure before calling LoadNode, excluding the candidate’s later fallback step.
The unchanged getter reads ctxt->errNo rather than the global error.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: The encoded limit and entity framing permit the selected XInclude allocation failure.
The installed allocator fails once at the encoded allocation ordinal and records the failure flag.
The existing failure check aborts when its expected result differs from the recorded allocation failure.

claims.comparison_reason: The same old harness and NewRef failure route apply on both sides. The old helper sets context errNo; the new helper does not. The candidate’s no-fallback clause is not part of this route because NewRef failure exits before LoadNode.

claims.necessity_reason: The reviewed target-coverage obligation is frozen as necessary; this claim assesses when its route became available.

before.requirement: Exercise a per-context XInclude structured error handler.
before.reason: The preimage context has no handler or handler-data fields, xmlXIncludeErr passes a null structured channel, and the preimage has no xmlXIncludeSetErrorHandler definition. The requested per-context route was therefore unavailable.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: The old included-document parser setup has no XInclude context-handler forwarding call.
The old XPointer context setup has no XInclude context-handler forwarding call.

after.requirement: Register a structured handler and data on the target’s XInclude context, then process an include that raises an XInclude error through that handler.
after.reason: The added setter populates context handler fields and xmlXIncludeErr passes them to the error dispatcher. The unchanged harness creates the context and calls SetFlags and ProcessNode without calling the setter, so every input leaves the new per-context route unselected.

source_evidence.dependency_reason: An unsupported parse value supplies an XInclude error on the target’s existing processing route.
Context creation zero-initializes the new handler field until the setter is called.

harness_evidence.dependency_reason: Initialization installs a global generic error handler, which does not set the XInclude context handler field.

claims.comparison_reason: The old harness call sequence is identical across versions. Before the change there was no per-context handler route to cover; afterward the route exists but requires a setter call that the harness never makes.
